                    case .audio(let content):
                        ReplyView(sender: sender,
                                  plainBody: content.caption ?? content.filename,
                                  formattedBody: content.formattedCaption,

                              plainBody: L10n.commonSharedLiveLocation,

Here's the full picture of how unavailable reply payloads are handled:

## Reply payload unavailability flow

### SDK → Factory ([RoomTimelineItemFactory.swift:844-885](ElementX/Sources/Services/Timeline/TimelineItems/RoomTimelineItemFactory.swift#L844-L885))

`buildTimelineItemReply` switches on `details.event()`, which is the Rust SDK's `InReplyToDetails`. There are four cases:

| SDK case | App `TimelineItemReplyDetails` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `.unavailable` | `.notLoaded(eventID:)` | Event not in local store — was never fetched |
| `.pending` | `.loading(eventID:)` | Being fetched right now |
| `.ready(...)` | `.loaded(sender:eventID:eventContent:)` | Full content available |
| `.error(message:)` | `.error(eventID:message:)` | Fetch failed |

### View layer ([TimelineReplyView.swift:38-115](ElementX/Sources/Screens/Timeline/View/Replies/TimelineReplyView.swift#L38-L115))

The view switches on `timelineItemReplyDetails`. The `.loaded` case renders the full reply preview. **Everything else** (`.notLoaded`, `.loading`, `.error`) falls through to the `default:` branch which renders `LoadingReplyView` — a redacted/shimmer placeholder using `.redacted(reason: .placeholder)` with the accessibility label `L10n.commonLoading`.

So when the reply content is unavailable, the UI shows a greyed-out shimmer placeholder rather than an error state or nothing. There's no explicit "reply not found" error shown to the user — `.error` and `.notLoaded` are both treated visually the same as `.loading`.
